header.name: Quantum Materials and Devices
header.description: The purpose of this course is to develop a broader understanding of beyond-CMOS electronic devices. It will introduce students to the rapidly developing field of quantum materials and devices, specifically the fundamental role of quantum physics in modern electronic, spintronic and molecular devices for both logic and memory applications. It will also highlight ongoing research on possible alternatives and novel materials for these advanced devices.
prerequisites_mandatory: Basic Knowledge on semiconductor device physics

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: The students will be able to describe the basic concepts involved in this technology for device architecture and interface engineering at the atomic limit.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: The students will understand low-dimensional mateials and devices. Explain the need of quantum mechanics in beyond-CMOS devices.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: The students will be able to describe different types of quantum electronic devices and their theoretical frameworks.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: The students will be able to describe different types of spintronic and molecular devices and their theoretical frameworks.

lecture_topics: Introduction - quantum effects as limitation to the miniaturization
tunneling through a general potential barrier
coherent and incoherent tunneling in series barriers
concepts of angular momentum - orbital angular momentum, spin angular momentum
spin state of two electron system
Quantum devices - tunnel juntion and tunnel diode
hetero structure based devices – Type I, II and III heterojunction
spin dynamical properties of magnetic materials
Emerging Spintronic Memories – STT-MRAM, SOT-MRAM, ME-MRAM, DW-motion MRAM, etc.
molecular orbital theory - concept of HOMO and LUMO, band gap etc.
